summary: At 08:56 portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) shipped a new "realised P&L" query reading ledger-db's trades table with no supporting index ("no migration included"). The query does sequential scans over 48.2M rows, driving ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96% and slow-query rate from ~1/min to ~140/min, and connections_active from ~62 to ~190. ledger-db is a shared datastore also used by order-service; with the DB CPU-saturated, order-service's INSERT INTO orders hits statement timeouts, producing p99 ~5.2s (vs ~150ms baseline) and ~9.5% 5xx beginning 08:49-09:00. order-service itself was not deployed this week and its own request rate is flat, so the fault originates in the portfolio-service release, not at order-service nor the DBA's autovacuum config change (which predates onset by ~45min and shows no independent signature). Historical incident HIST-111 is the same pattern.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service v4.5.0 unindexed trades query saturates shared ledger-db, timing out order-service INSERTs
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5905 deployed at 08:56 added a realised-P&L query on ledger-db's trades table (WHERE account_id + executed_at ORDER BY executed_at) with no supporting index ('no migration included'). It does 48.2M-row sequential scans at ~140/min, pushing ledger-db CPU from ~30% to ~96% and active connections from ~62 to ~190. Because ledger-db is shared, order-service's INSERT INTO orders contends for the same saturated instance and hits statement timeouts, producing p99 ~5.2s and ~9.5% 5xx from ~08:49-09:00.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5905 ships a new trades query with no index
Query runs 48.2M-row seq scans, ~140 slow queries/min, 7459-8391ms each
Shared ledger-db saturated -> order-service INSERT INTO orders exceeds statement timeout

assumptions: ledger-db is a single instance shared by portfolio-service and order-service (shared:true implies co-location)
the slow-query warnings reported by ledger-db accurately attribute load to portfolio-service
order-service uses the same ledger-db endpoint that portfolio-service's new query hits

ranked_hypotheses.title: DBA autovacuum config change on ledger-db caused the slowdown
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2903 changed ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor from 0.2 to 0.1 at 08:00, more aggressive autovacuum, which the incident report flags. This is rejected: it was applied ~45-49min before onset, the only autovacuum activity in logs targets public.audit_log (not trades), no vacuum errors exist, and the ledger-db CPU/slow-query pattern is dominated by portfolio-service's unindexed SELECT rather than maintenance work.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Config applied at 08:00 but symptoms began 08:45-08:58; autovacuum logs show only audit_log processing and no vacuum/IO signature on trades; slow-query logs explicitly attribute the heavy scans to application_name=portfolio-service, which deployed at 08:56.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation of ledger-db under a traffic increase
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Alternative that order-service/ledger-db simply ran out of headroom under rising load. Rejected because order-service request_rate is flat (~225-235 req/s) across the window and ledger-db CPU was steady at ~30% before 08:45, so the load did not grow organically; the extra load appeared only with the new portfolio-service query.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate flat (F11) and pre-onset DB CPU stable at ~30% (F7) rule out organic load growth as the trigger.

facts.statement: order-service p99 jumped from ~150ms to ~5200ms (max 5768ms) with onset in the 08:49 bucket.
order-service errors rose to ~9.5% 5xx coincident with the latency jump.
All order-service errors are 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)' against ledger-db.
ledger-db's dominant slow query is a 48.2M-row Seq Scan on trades attributed to application_name=portfolio-service.
portfolio-service v4.5.0 deployed at 08:56 with a new trades query and no migration (no index).
ledger-db CPU rose from ~30% to ~96% at onset.
ledger-db active connections rose from ~62 to ~190.
order-service DB pool usage rose from ~14 to ~46 waiting connections.
order-service request rate was flat throughout, ruling out a traffic surge.
The autovacuum config change cfg-2903 was applied at 08:00, ~45min before onset, and post-change autovacuum only touched public.audit_log.
ledger-db disk usage (~71%) and replication lag (~40ms) were flat, ruling out disk/replication faults.
ledger-db is a shared datastore that order-service depends on.
A prior incident (HIST-111) had the same pattern: an unindexed report query doing seq scans slowed ledger-db.

assumptions: ledger-db is a single shared Postgres instance serving both portfolio-service and order-service (shared:true implies co-location)
ledger-db slow-query log attribution of application_name=portfolio-service is accurate
order-service's INSERT INTO orders targets the same ledger-db instance that the portfolio-service query hits
latency_p99/error_rate metrics are end-to-end for order-service as reported

timeline.event: Last healthy bucket: order-service p99 ~151ms, ledger-db CPU ~30%, slow queries ~0.9/min
Degradation onset: order-service p99 1358ms; ledger-db CPU 50% avg, slow queries 44.9/min; connections rising
portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) deployed; new unindexed trades query
First ledger-db slow-query warning: 8690ms Seq Scan on trades, application_name=portfolio-service
First portfolio-service 'holdings P&L query took 7459ms' warning
First order-service INSERT INTO orders statement timeout
Steady-state failure: ledger-db CPU ~96%, slow queries ~140/min, connections ~190; order-service p99 ~5300ms, errors ~9.5%
Incident still ongoing at end of data window

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or hotfix portfolio-service v4.5.0 (dep-5905) to stop the unindexed trades query, or disable the realised-P&L code path via feature flag
recommended_actions.rationale: The new query is the load source driving ledger-db saturation; removing it should relieve order-service timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Add an index on trades(account_id, executed_at) (or (executed_at, account_id)) to eliminate the 48.2M-row sequential scan before re-enabling the query
recommended_actions.rationale: The Seq Scan on trades is the direct cost driver; an index converts it to an index range scan.

recommended_actions.action: Verify immediate recovery: order-service p99 back to ~150ms, error rate to ~0.2%, ledger-db CPU back to ~30%, slow_queries_per_min back to ~1/min
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the causal chain and that no other fault remains.

recommended_actions.action: Add a mandatory query-review/index-check gate and statement_timeout/rate limits for heavy analytical queries against shared ledger-db
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence; mirrors HIST-111's resolution ('Added index; query review gate').

recommended_actions.action: Reassess autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor change separately; it is not the cause but its interaction with heavy scans on trades should be reviewed
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2903 is a distractor for this incident but the DBA change context should be closed out.

data_gaps: No direct evidence of a missing index on trades (schema/index listing not available); inference rests on the 'Seq Scan on trades (rows=48211907)' plan annotation and the 'no migration included' deployment note.
ledger-db has no per-application or per-statement breakdown metrics beyond the slow-query log, so the exact share of CPU attributable to portfolio-service vs order-service cannot be quantified.
No ready signal for whether a rollback of dep-5905 was attempted during the window (rollback status is null = not rolled back).
The reported 'DBA changed autovacuum settings this morning' is only corroborated by cfg-2903; no I/O or bloat metric specific to trades is available to fully exclude any autovacuum side effect.

findings.statement: order-service p99 latency was flat ~150ms through 08:36, jumped to 1358ms avg at 08:49 and settled ~5200ms (max 5768ms) from 09:02 onward.
order-service error rate rose from ~0.2% to 9.46% avg (max 10.0) beginning in the 08:49 bucket alongside the latency jump.
order-service logs show 284 ERROR entries, all the single pattern 'canceling statement due to statement timeout (INSERT INTO orders)', first seen 09:00:42 and continuing to 10:58:29.

findings.statement: ledger-db CPU was ~30% through 08:36, then rose to avg 95.73/max 97.58 at 09:02 and stayed ~96% thereafter.
ledger-db slow_queries_per_min was ~1.0/min through 08:36, then 44.91 avg/max 148.81 at 08:49 and ~140/min (max 153.27) from 09:02 onward.
ledger-db connections_active rose from ~62 through 08:36 to avg 189.54 (max 199.85) at 09:02 and remained ~190-197.
order-service db_pool_in_use rose from ~14 through 08:36 to avg 46.39 (max 51.63) at 09:02, indicating connections blocked waiting on the DB.
order-service request_rate was essentially flat (~225-235 req/s) across the entire window, so the degradation is not caused by a traffic surge.
Config change cfg-2903 changed ledger-db autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor from 0.2 to 0.1 at 08:00:00Z ('More aggressive autovacuum') and was applied/logged at 08:00:20.
ledger-db autovacuum activity after cfg-2903 was on table public.audit_log only; no autovacuum or vacuum error entries mention the trades table.
No deployments were recorded for order-service or ledger-db in the window; the only deployment across all services was dep-5905 on portfolio-service.
ledger-db disk_used_pct was flat ~71% and replication_lag_ms flat ~40ms throughout, so disk exhaustion and replication lag are not factors.
order-service depends on ledger-db (kind db), and ledger-db is flagged shared:true (used by several services).

The unindexed portfolio-service query and order-service's INSERT into the same ledger-db instance are co-located, so the query's CPU/IO consumption on ledger-db is the mechanism degrading order-service.
